description.narrative: Stora delar av Asien och Stillahavsområdet ligger i framkant när det gäller modern global utveckling och blir allt mer ekonomiskt integrerat, och dessutom allt närmare sammanlänkat genom en komplex väv av vägar, järnvägar, vattenkraftsdammar, ekonomiska zoner, energinät, exploatering av naturresurser och leveranskedjor för jordbruksprodukter. Detta skapar ekonomiska möjligheter för samhällen, länder och dess omvärld, men det medför också risker. Som ett resultat av covid-19-pandemin står regionen dessutom inför ökade sociala, ekonomiska och miljömässiga utmaningar, vilket sätter ytterligare press på utsatta grupper. Det ohållbara utnyttjandet av skogslandskapen i regionen sker genom icke-transparenta styrmekanismer och ekonomiska intressen. Skogarna i regionen hotas av denna utveckling, men skogarna är också en stor del av lösningen. Skogen reglerar ekosystemen, skyddar den biologiska mångfalden, spelar en viktig roll i kolets kretslopp, stabiliserar klimatet, stöder människors försörjning och kan bidra till att driva på en hållbar tillväxt. När en skog förvaltas på ett hållbart sätt kan den avsevärt förbättra motståndskraften hos både ekosystem och samhällen. För att fortsätta sitt arbete i skogslandskap och för att möta dessa behov och utmaningar utvecklade RECOFTC den strategiska planen 2023-2028, som syftar till att bidra till positiva resultat för människor, skogar och ekosystem i RECOFTC:s fokusländer och prioriterade landskap genom framsteg mot fyra sammanlänkade mål relaterade till klimatförändringar, jämställdhet och social integration, styrning och rättigheter samt samhällsnytta. Huvudfokus är att stärka kapacitet, rättigheter och styrning för att säkerställa att lokalbefolkningen kan upprätthålla och dra nytta av hållbara skogslandskap i Asien och Stillahavsområdet. Ambassaden bedömer att insatsen är i linje med målen och i Sveriges strategi för regionalt utvecklingssamarbete i Asien och Stillahavsområdet 2022-2026, genom att den främjar hållbar skogsförvaltning med fokus på mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet, fattiga människor och en hållbar miljö.

The Asia-Pacific region, which is at the forefront of modern global development, is becoming more economically integrated, as well as more closely linked through a complex web of roads, rail, hydropower dams, economic zones, energy grids, natural resource exploitation, and agricultural supply chains. This creates economic opportunities for communities, countries, and beyond, but it also carries unsettling risks. Moreover, as a result of the Covid-19 pandemic, the region is facing increased social, economic, and environmental challenges, putting additional pressure on vulnerable groups. The unsustainable exploitation of forest landscapes in the region takes place amongst opaque governance mechanisms and financial interests. Forests in the region are threatened by each of these trends and related trade-offs, but forests are a big part of the solutions too. Forest regulate ecosystems, protect biodiversity, play an important role in the carbon cycle, stabilize the climate, support livelihoods, and can help drive sustainable growth. When a forest is managed sustainably, it can significantly improve the resilience of both ecosystems and societies.
To continue its work in forest landscapes and to meet those needs and challenges, RECOFTC developed the Strategic Plan 2023-2028, which aims to contribute to positive outcomes for people, forests, and ecosystems in RECOFTC focal countries and priority landscapes through progress toward four linked goals related to climate change, gender equality and social inclusion, governance and rights, and community benefits. The key focus is to strengthen capacities, rights and governance to ensure that local people can maintain and benefit equitably from sustainable forest landscapes in the Asia-Pacific region. The Embassy assesses that the intervention is in line with the objectives and theory of change of Sweden's Regional Development Cooperation Strategy in Asia and the Pacific 2022-2026, which promotes for sustainable forest management in the region through a method that incorporates aspects for human rights, gender equality, poor people, and the environment.

The overall impact of the Strategic Plan 2023-2028 is that resilient communities sustainably and equitably manage forest landscapes in collaboration with other stakeholders, ensuring that these landscapes provide goods and services that benefit all community members and wider populations, including by contributing to climate action and biodiversity conservation. This will be achieved through the interlinked four goals, which are:
Goal 1 - Enhanced climate change adaptation and mitigation;
Goal 2 - Improved gender equality and social inclusion;
Goal 3 - Improved governance and respect for rights; and
Goal 4 - Increased economic benefits for communities.
There are six mutually reinforcing strategies that will help RECOFTC achieve its desired goals, outcomes, and impact, which are as follows:
1) Ensuring that forest landscapes provide climate solutions
2) Secures rights and inclusive governance
3) Supports growth of forest-landscape-related businesses
4) Secures finance for sustainable forest landscapes
5) Generates evidence for influence
6) Engages the public on forest landscape issues

RECOFTCs progress under its four strategic goals: climate change adaptation and mitigation, gender equality and social inclusion, governance and rights, and economic benefits for communities. Based on annual operational report (Sept 2023 to Oct 2024), the key results under each goal are:
1. Enhanced Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation:
- Carbon Sequestration: Over 200 million tons of CO equivalent sequestered in priority landscapes.
- Climate and Conservation Financing: Initiated 12 projects receiving or preparing to receive carbon and biodiversity funding.
- Forest Landscape Vulnerability Assessments: Conducted three assessments in Thailand and Nepal to support nature-based solutions (NbS).
- Community Capacity Development, include: i) 80,869 people (50% women) benefited from climate adaptation measures; ii) Conducted 22 capacity-building sessions to help communities participate in carbon projects; and iii) Supported forest fire prevention initiatives in Laos and Thailand, resulting in fire management plans and over 20 km of firebreaks created.
2. Improved Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI):
- Gender-Responsive Policies: 7 gender-sensitive policies and plans developed and adopted at national and subnational levels in Cambodia, Indonesia, Thailand, and at the regional level.
- Capacity Development on Gender Equality: 1,453 people trained in gender integration in forestry and climate initiatives. Conducted 10 online gender mainstreaming courses in Indonesia, engaging 1,068 participants.
- Leadership & Networking: Launched Phase 2 of the WAVES program, training 21 young gender leaders in climate advocacy.
3. Improved Governance and Respect for Rights:
- Legal & Policy Reforms: Supported the development and adoption of 13 national and subnational laws and policies related to natural resource management and climate governance. For example, facilitateMini Trust Fund and Community Forestry Credit Scheme guidelines in Cambodia, and support technical guidelines for village forest management planning and forest fire prevention in Lao PDR.
- Community Forest & Land Tenure: Secured forest land tenure for 8,215 people in Cambodia and Vietnam.
4. Increased Economic Benefits for Communities:
- Community-Based Enterprises (CBEs) & Livelihoods: Supported 40 CBEs, including 21 individual enterprises and 22 group enterprises.Expanded 6 enterprises in Indonesia, Nepal, and Thailand through market access support and networking.
- Market & Financial Access: Facilitated responsible lending practices for 151 community members.Developed new agroforestry models in Indonesia and Lao PDR.
- Private Sector Engagement: 9 private sector actors improved business practices to promote responsible investments.
- Capacity Development: Conducted 23 training sessions on sustainability, financial management, and business partnerships.
Results at regional level:
At the regional level, RECOFTC focused on enhancing climate adaptation, governance, gender equality, and economic benefits across its seven focal countries, key results include:
- In climate change adaptation and mitigation, the organization supported 12 carbon and biodiversity financing projects, contributing to over 200 million tons of CO sequestration. RECOFTC also published six knowledge products emphasizing the role of Indigenous Peoples (IPs) and Local Communities (LCs) in national climate commitments.
- In gender equality and social inclusion (GESI), RECOFTC played a key role in integrating gender in forestry and climate governance, supporting Cambodias Neary Rattanak VI Strategic Plan 20242028 and assisting Indonesias Ministry of Environment and Forestry in launching gender equality guidelines for forestry courses. The WAVES Phase 2 program was launched to train 21 young gender leaders across the region in climate and environmental justice. Capacity development efforts benefited 1,453 people, including 1,068 participants in Indonesias online gender mainstreaming courses and 129 individuals in Vietnam trained in forest fire management. Womens leadership in community forestry planning was also strengthened in Thailand, Cambodia, and Nepal.
- In governance and rights, RECOFTC contributed to the development of 13 national and subnational legal frameworks, including participatory forest and land allocation policies in Cambodia and Vietnam, securing forest tenure for 8,215 people. The organization also enhanced governance safeguards such as Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) and dispute resolution mechanisms for 165 stakeholders, including governments and private sector actors. Furthermore, RECOFTC engaged in 26 national and subnational networks to advance sustainable forest governance and trained 695 people in policy advocacy and community rights.
- Economic benefits for communities were also a key focus, with RECOFTC supporting 40 community-based enterprises (CBEs) in product development, financial access, and market linkages. Among the CBEs that RECOFTC worked with and supported, six enterprises in Indonesia, Nepal and Thailand have increased their memberships, including newly registered enterprises and expanded their network and partnership. Additionally, responsible lending practices were facilitated for 151 community members in Lao PDR, Myanmar, and Thailand, while nine private sector actors adopted responsible investment approaches.
